newsitem.title: USA: Ralph Lauren seeks to raise about $700 mln in IPO.
newsitem.headline: Ralph Lauren seeks to raise about $700 mln in IPO.

text.p: Polo Ralph Lauren Corp's initial public offering terms have been set at 29.5 million shares with a pricing range of $22 to $25 a share, according to a filing, dated May 21, with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission.
At a midpoint price of $23.50, this gives the New York-based designer's deal a value of almost $700 million.
Of the 29.5 million shares, 23.5 million are slated for the United States and six million will be sold in an international offering.

The company is selling 9.4 million shares and the other 20.1 million are being offered by selling stockholders. These include, according to the filing, Ralph Lauren, possibly a Lauren family trust and immediate family members, and the GS Group -- comprising affiliates of investment bank Goldman, Sachs & Co.
Goldman Sachs, also lead underwriter on the deal, owns 28 percent of Ralph Lauren.
The company proposes to trade on the New York Stock Exchange under the symbol RL.N.
